newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower on stock slide.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower on stock slide.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Friday after repeatedly failing to test the upside as Tokyo stocks were dragged down by weakness in the financial and construction sectors, dealers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract lost 215 points to end at 17,880 after falling to a low of 17,750. Market turnover was a thin 14,880 lots.
A trader with a Japanese house said the market drifted down after follow-through buying failed to emerge on the back of a large buy order on Tokyo's TOPIX share index.
"I think the market will go lower from here since 18,200 has been a very strong resistance," he said.
Dealers said the market could take its cue next week from Wall Street's reaction to the U.S. non-farm payrolls report for March, due at 1330 GMT.

"The Dow could come under pressure if these figures are more inflationary than expected. And if the Fed (Federal Reserve) has to hike rates a second time, it will give the Bank of Japan a reason to move once," a trader with a local institution said.
